object.title: The Horse Fair
object.pick_reason: At nearly 17 feet wide, this monumental masterpiece was created by Rosa Bonheur, who famously had to obtain a police 'cross-dressing permit' to sketch at the all-male Paris horse markets unnoticed.

script: She needed a police permit just to wear pants here. To paint this massive 17-foot canvas in the 1850s, Rosa Bonheur had to get official permission from the French police to dress in men’s clothes. Why? Because women weren't allowed at the Paris horse market, and she needed to blend in with the rowdy crowd. And honestly? It totally paid off. Look at the chaotic energy of these horses. That rearing white stallion in the center practically leaps right at you. You can almost hear the thundering hooves and smell the dust kicked up in the air. Bonheur spent over a year sketching here, getting every single muscle flex and wild eye down perfectly. Wait, look closely at this rider in the blue cap right in the center of the madness. See how they're looking directly at us while everyone else is struggling with the animals? Many believe that's actually Rosa herself, hiding in plain sight. She spent eighteen months on this giant painting, and it made her a global superstar. Would you break the law for your art?
